key_insight: Private score estimation achieves a nearly minimax-optimal privacy–accuracy trade-off and enables diffusion models whose privacy guarantee is independent of denoising-step count.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a theoretically grounded route to privacy-preserving generative modeling, with a score-estimation algorithm whose runtime is polynomial in sample size.
method: Represent scores using quadratic B-splines and sample private estimates via the exponential mechanism.
Implement sampling with projected Langevin Monte Carlo under sub-Gaussian and local Hölder-smoothness assumptions.
Use private score estimates in a discretized diffusion model with nearly minimax-optimal expected total variation error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a nearly matching minimax lower bound and experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, but gives no numerical results.
watch_item: Polynomial runtime does not establish practical scalability; performance also depends on the stated distributional assumptions and an appropriate diffusion discretization.
paper_title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
